# ML Knowledge / Discussion Round

[← DoorDash](../README.md) · [Every DoorDash question](../../doordash.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/mle-ml-discussion-round)

`ab-testing` `experiment-design` `ml-knowledge` `ranking` `verbal`

---

## Requirements

- Broad machine-learning discussion with no coding.
- Typical interviewer topics:
  - A/B testing basics: forming hypotheses, calculating statistical power, reducing variance with CUPED, and reading confidence intervals.
  - Designing ranking metrics: CTR versus CVR versus revenue per session, along with offline NDCG / AUC versus online conversion.
  - Ranking for multiple objectives: merging business signals such as CVR, delivery time, freshness, and ad placements within one ranker.
  - Marketplace experimentation: choosing switchbacks or A/B tests for marketplace effects, identifying novelty effects, and selecting guard-rail metrics.
  - The offline-to-online gap: reasons an offline improvement failed to launch successfully online, including data leakage and feature-serving skew.
  - Observing and troubleshooting ML systems.
  - Techniques from the candidate's own recent projects, followed by questions about why they were selected and how they performed after launch.
- The interviewer controls the discussion, while the candidate is expected to show broad applied-ML knowledge.

## Notes

- DoorDash places more emphasis on marketplace considerations than most comparable companies; switchback design, supply-demand elasticity, and treatment effects by region may receive specific attention.
- A two-head ranker is the standard response for multi-objective ranking, though the interviewer may follow up by asking about a joint loss.
- A/B testing is covered at unusual depth for an MLE interview. Review power calculations, MDE, and variance-reduction methods.
- A frequent weakness is giving superficial treatment to reconciling offline and online metrics. Prepare a concrete example in which an offline metric rose but the online metric did not, including what the investigation uncovered.
- Some interviewers come from non-ML backgrounds, such as backend engineering, and may ask ML questions; responses might need less formalism and more intuition. Adjust to the audience.
- The PhD-intern process uses a lighter “ML case analysis” form of this discussion as one of its two VOs: it tests the same breadth of applied-ML understanding with less depth.
- Recent Senior MLE loops may frame this as a resume-based domain-knowledge discussion: be ready to explain which methods you applied, why they suited the product problem, and where the model or experiment broke down.

## Preparation

- Prepare three stories in advance: (1) an A/B test you planned and launched, (2) a ranking model released with both offline and online metrics, and (3) a divergence between offline and online metrics together with its root cause.
- Review switchback experiments using a standard reference, such as the Statsig blog or a comparable industry post-mortem.
- Rehearse explaining the trade-offs in multi-objective ranking, including two heads plus lambda and joint loss as an alternative, in less than two minutes.
- Keep two or three marketplace-focused examples available, such as dasher allocation, surge, and restaurant ranking; DoorDash interviewers value intuition tied to the domain.
